From terrible gameplay and hitboxes over motion sickness (in a 3rd person game?????) all the way to a story even more confusing than any soulsborne game, this game is a mess. I refunded this once already because I hated the weirdly placed and highly restrictive invisible walls but decided to give it a 2nd shot. I can now say that I wholeheartedly regret spending that much money on a game I probably won't continue playing. 
The gameplay is sluggish. Animations are way to long with an input buffer that extends these periods even further making your life harder. Animation cancels are non existent. A dodge with 3 progressively longer animations looks cool but is impractical as hell. You're reliant on it tho, since there aren't real parries (there's a spell that kinda parries but there's a cooldown on it and it relies on mana which you can't refill until you rest. horrible design choice). There are 1000 different things to choose from in the skill tree which leaves you in a choice paralysis until you realize that most of these things are utter garbage you won't use anyway. There are stances which you can unlock by spending points which don't seem to offer any benefit at all. So why even bother???
Then there's the difficulty curve. The main areas are easy, every casual gamer should be able to breeze through there. I cleared everything unti I hit the final boss - a roadblock akin to Ornstein & Smough in DS1. Which truly made me think: where does BM:W want to position itself? That boss was annoying as hell because of the aforementioned things already but on top of it it had the biggest healthbar up until that point. And because he left very few openings, the battle was long. So if I was a casual gamer who managed to clear the game up until there, wtf am I supposed to do? You're >8h in atp, so you can't even refund. 
The next boss (which made me write this rant-y review) was the first one in the next area. It instantly one-hitted me with an attack. When I went in again I had to find out that the camera was playing against you because the boss was hardly in focus while most hits were a whiff due to the horrendous hitboxes. (I even ran into some enemies that weren't able to hit me despite standing literally inside me...) And since that boss was BIG, you had to run miles to get to the body parts you were able to hit. But until you reached that, he was on the run already. While I could use some spells, as I already mentioned, mana is laughably limited with no option to replenish mid fight. He also just walzes right through most attempts of "parrying/blocking", so that's some mana wasted. I didn't even try to fight him more than 5 times because I'm already pissed off beyond belief at this points.
Which is quite a shame because the visuals are GREAT, the game just does close to nothing with them. The world looks extremely cool and engaging but all you do is walk and fight, close to no interactions with anything whatsoever. The story could also be quite cool, especially the cutscenes seem great most times, but it feels very directionless. I don't even know the name of the protagonist, let alone what his main goal is. All I do is walk and fight. And those two are some of the weakest points of the game

I genuinely haven't had this much fun with a game in a while. Black Myth: Wukong was exactly what I needed, a great mix of soulslike and hack-and-slash combat, with a beautiful world, interesting bosses, and gameplay that kept me hooked.

The combat feels amazing. It's fast, satisfying, and there's enough variety in the abilities to experiment with different playstyles. But the bosses were definitely my favorite part. There are so many of them, and each one feels different. Some took me quite a few attempts to beat, but instead of getting frustrated, I usually just wanted to try again. And finally beating a boss after struggling for a while? That's exactly the feeling I love about soulslike games.

I also really enjoyed the world and its atmosphere. Chinese mythology looks absolutely gorgeous here, and some locations are so beautiful that I actually stopped just to look around. The side quests, hidden bosses, and secret areas were another pleasant surprise. I love games that don't constantly hold your hand and actually reward you for exploring.

Another thing I appreciated was how smooth the controls and camera felt. Even during difficult fights, I could focus on the boss instead of fighting against the game itself.

Overall, I had an amazing time playing it. For me, it's easily one of the best games that combines soulslike elements with hack-and-slash combat. It has pretty much everything I enjoy: challenging and spectacular bosses, rewarding exploration, a beautiful atmosphere, and a combat system that stays fun even after dozens of hours.
Definitely recommend it. I'd honestly love to play through it all over again.

Black Myth: Wukong is easily one of the most memorable gaming experiences I’ve had. As someone playing their first Souls-like game, I wasn’t sure what to expect going in, but this game completely won me over.

The storytelling and world-building are absolutely incredible. The way the game brings Chinese mythology to life, with its mysterious characters, legendary creatures, and fascinating lore, kept me wanting to explore more and discover what awaited me around every corner.

The visuals are breathtaking. From stunning landscapes and ancient temples to dark caves, snowy mountains, and massive boss arenas, every location feels beautifully crafted. There were so many moments when I just stopped to admire the scenery.

And the combat is where the game truly shines. The boss fights are challenging, intense, and incredibly satisfying. Every defeat teaches you something, and finally taking down a boss you’ve been struggling with feels amazing. As a newcomer to the Souls-like genre, the learning curve was tough at times, but that feeling of progression made every victory worth it.

What I love most is how the game combines exploration, challenging combat, mythology, and cinematic moments into one incredible adventure. It can be frustrating sometimes, but it rarely takes away from the excitement of finally overcoming a difficult challenge.

My verdict: An absolute masterpiece of an action RPG that delivers an unforgettable adventure. The story, visuals, music, and combat make it well worth experiencing, even if you're new to Souls-like games.

This is my first Souls-like journey, and Black Myth: Wukong has set the bar incredibly high. If this is what the genre has to offer, I can’t wait to experience more games like it.

Self Experience and Insights:
Growing up as a child who's obsessed with Journey to the West, this is the bleakest version that matches the originally intended critique to the corrupted bureaucratic dynasty.

We idolise and even worship Wukong as a deity in Chinese's Taoism + Buddhism hybrid belief system in South East Asia, China and Taiwan, even though he's actually a fictional mythology character intended for satire.

Being a child I used to think Wukong is cool and "punk" for being a character who has no burden and care for Heaven and Earth, challenging the system that's being unfair and rigid to someone as free as him. But after playing this game, it hits a now grown-up me in a realistic level, that Wukong, an idolised figure who's deemed to be invincible and flexibly powerful, could be just another replaceable pawn to be sacrificed in a broken system manipulated by those in real power. It feels both unnerving and enlightening at the same time.

Opinion on Game itself:
1st ever 3A game by an Indie studio who has little to none prior experience in this genre and development experience. Imagine the cut content they have to give up for this game to launch as planned, and still able to keep the quality and consistency this much for players. 

- Weaving unlockable skills throughout the story is really immersive, the secrets and side stories feels equally impactful as the main one, and some even have heart-wrenching moments knowing the lore from a Chinese mythology enthusiast's perspective.
- Combats are rewarding with the monsters and boss fights, but the consistency between bosses may feel unevenly too strong or weak.
- The equipment have their own unique builds and very well designed in terms of ancient mythical aesthetics, adding to the replayability to keep unlocking to see how cool looking it gets gradually and feel their unique strength.
- The soundtracks are orchestrated beautifully to match with each settings such as combat, map, cutscenes and even the savepoint. Personally I would collect the vinyls for the soundtrack if they would release one. Shoutout to Yellow Wind Ridge's Shaanbei storytelling tracks.
- Whole experience can feel inspired from God of War and Ghost of Tsushima, which also shares the similar mythological settings and combat experience with the former, while sharing stances system and ancient asian aesthetics from nature environments to armory with the latter.

Overall a game which does great in balancing both story and gameplay, giving Journey to the West its well-deserved treatment as a game, a true art of culture celebration for one of the greatest masterpieces of Chinese literature.

I was going to write this review weeks after the game's release, but let's just say a long Hiatus was taken and I essentially forgot about the game (reason will be said why).
So Black Myth : Wukong...is a great game, initially I was skeptical, since the more I kept playing, the more harder it got (though partially because my dumbass didn't explore enough to find out I could craft celestial medicines). Note that this Review will contain spoilers.

Gameplay 9/10 : The Fighting System is a bit of a mix from God of War but also your average Hack N Slash games. Exploration in this game is huge, practically a ,Metroidvania, thus why this game could be considered a Souls game. This game also has a big ass kit, ranging from Stances, to Spirit attacks, to Transformations and Spells. Also comes with a huge skill tree that makes the combat system more flexible. Overall pretty good, tho later bosses can be a huge pain, that Perfect Dodging quite often is required.

Chapter 1 : Cool Beginning
It's a great start of a game. It's beautiful, it gives you the fundamentals of combat, and the bosses are not too challenging. Especially the final boss of the Chapter, the Black Bear, it's quite epic.

Chapter 2 : A step down
I did not really enjoy it much, mainly because the Area had all these rock enemies that can really be annoying early game, but mostly cause of the bosses. All of a sudden you got a duo boss that really claps your ass into oblivion, and then the final boss of the Chapter has an unfair Tornado Wall that you can just accidentally run into, whilst the boss himself can just camp there, literally. Overall not the best.

Chapter 3 : Atrocity
I hated every second of this chapter, it's the longest of the 6, and has one of, if not, the most frustrating bosses ever made in Gaming. I despise Yellowbrow's fight with every atom of my being, due to his random non-pattern Golden Form that can just trigger mid-immobilize, and literally thanks to lightning, his attacks are just not dodgeable. Literally after I beat him, I then thought the game is just gonna get worse if I keep playing, thus why I didn't play it for a long time.

Chapter 4 : A step up
This one surprised me, it had an interesting beginning, middle, but a very bad end. The Chapter is probably the 2nd shortest, but it's the most beautiful I'd say, mainly cause of the secret area. The Final boss of the chapter though...yeah no, it's not a good one.

Chapter 5 : Redemption
This is without a shadow of a doubt, my favorite chapter of them all. I loved the area, I loved the bosses, and especially the final boss of the chapter, which was the Yaksha King, literally whoever came up with the design and fight, give em a raise.

Chapter 6 : Great Conclusion
I loved that this one you can ride the nimbus, it makes exploration be on a whole different level, but I liked the progression of the chapter, it is the shortest of them. The FInal boss was also one of the greatest fights I've ever seen in Gaming.

Issues I had with the game : For people who are playing on Laptops, yeah no fullscreen on this game, which can really be a problem. This game also suffers a bit from Input Lag, so don't be surprised if you keep trying to dodge a repeated attack but your character just doesen't or having to press the heal button twice in a row to heal. While the game has cool bosses, it also has bad one's, and they can be really bad too (I'm looking at you Cyan Loong Prince), so in short, boss Inconsistencies.

The Lore : 9/10
While it is an invented Chinese mythology story, it still references Journey to the West and I daresay even pays homage to it, whilst also having elements from Dark Souls' story a bit implemented. You, as the Destined One, gotta find 6 relics and fight what remains of Wukong to BECOME Wukong. However you will only find 5 of the relics, the 6th one is obtained from beating all major secret bosses. You fight Wukong's greatest rival, Erlang Shen, who arguably is harder. If you beat him, you get the Memories, and thus once you beat Wukong, you get the True Ending, where he finally is reborn/reincarnated, and refuses to wear the golden headband that once kept him under the Celestial Court's control.

Overall, I give this game a 8/10. For a first AAA game, I say Game Science did well, it's just that there are some inconsistencies regarding certain aspects of the game. For those who are into Chinese Mythology, and very much are Masochists/desire a Challenge to waste hours on, this game's pretty much for you.


P.S : This should've won GOTY honestly.

In a sentence: fantastic game BUT it has its flaws.

First of all, although it looks like it: this is not a Souls game. It's an action game with Souls-like elements. It has shrines where you can rest and recover your resources, along with a few other ideas borrowed from the genre, but you don't lose anything when you die, regular enemies aren't particularly difficult, and aside from a handful of bosses, the game is nowhere near as punishing as a traditional Souls game.

The skill tree is very good. There is plenty of room to customize your playstyle through skills, weapons, armor and equipment. I wouldn't call it revolutionary, but it's well designed and executed.

The bosses are probably the strongest part of the game. Each one has its own identity, design and story, which adds a lot of variety. There are a ridiculous number of them, and almost all of them have their own identity. I never felt like I was fighting the same enemy with a different skin, which I really appreciated. I beat most of them on my first try, although there were a few that made me retry several times.

The main problem with the game is the chapter structure. There are only six chapters, but the areas are quite large and can feel very long. Several times I found myself enjoying the game while also thinking, “Okay, when does this chapter end?” It's a strange feeling because I wasn't bored, but I definitely felt like the game could have been shorter. 

Personally, I think the game would have been better if it were about 10 hours shorter.

Chapter 6 is the clearest example. It's much more open, and while flying around on the cloud is spectacular, I think the level design is pretty terrible. The final fights are much better, though, and the secret ending is absolutely worth seeing.

I also really enjoyed the story. I wasn't particularly familiar with Journey to the West, so I came into the game knowing very little about it. Still, I think the way the game uses that material to build its own story works really well. The structure of moving forward, meeting characters, helping some of them and fighting others works nicely, and the story is carried more by its world and characters than by one huge central plot. The chapter bosses' backstories are also very good.

One thing that really annoyed me was the invisible walls. There are countless moments where the environment makes it look like you should be able to go somewhere, only for you to run into an invisible wall in the middle of nowhere. It happened far too many times.

Overall, I think this game is considerably better than its 81 on Metacritic. It has some design issues and is definitely longer than it needs to be, but the combat, bosses, progression, atmosphere and overall spectacle made it a game I really enjoyed.

Highly recommended, especially if you like action games with Souls-like elements. Just don't expect an actual Souls game.

[b][u]Triple-A Vaporware – A Brainless, Lifeless Tech Demo Masquerading as an Action Game[/u][/b]

Let’s strip away the corporate marketing hype and visual smoke mirrors: Black Myth: Wukong is a fundamentally broken, clunky, and utterly hollow experience. Before the fanboys rush to tell me to "get good," let's clear something up: I am no stranger to brutal difficulty. I have conquered Onimusha on Carnage mode, and I have fully beaten unforgiving high-precision games like Nine Sols. I love games that push my reflexes to the absolute limit. But those games are tough-but-fair; Wukong is just a masterclass in mechanical frustration and design incompetence.

Game Science has delivered a product that fails at basic game design on every conceivable level:
[list]
[*] [b]A "Combat" System Built on Clunky Delusions:[/b] The developers want you to think this is a precision action game. It isn't. The "See-Through" / Resolute Strike counter mechanic is a fraudulent joke. It is chained to a sluggish, unresponsive input-buffering queue that forces you to awkwardly prep a light attack before you can even attempt to parry. Worse, the invincibility frames are so pitifully brief that bosses with brainless multi-hit tracking will routinely smash you right out of your counter animation—even after the game’s own red-flash visual cue confirms you hit the frame-perfect window.

[*] [b]Abysmal Camera Work and Broken Physics:[/b] Fighting massive bosses like the Tiger Vanguard means fighting the camera, not the enemy. The perspective violently glues itself to the boss’s crotch, completely cutting off their upper body, shoulders, and arms from the screen. The game aggressively demands you react to visual cues that its own trash camera tracking refuses to let you see, leaving you staring at a blurry, zoomed-in wall of clipping pixels.

[*] [b]A Lifeless, Aggressive Theme Park:[/b] Outside of the muddy combat, the world design is a pathetic joke. The environments are completely dead, lifeless corridors padded out by a sickening amount of immersion-shattering invisible walls. You cannot explore; you can only walk down pre-baked hallways disguised as forests and deserts.

[*] [b]A Forgettable, Incoherent Narrative:[/b] For a game relying so heavily on classic mythology, the narrative delivery is entirely flat and unengaging. It gives you absolutely no compelling reason to care about the journey, dropping the ball on pacing and character motivation right out of the gate.

[*] [b]Artificial Difficulty Over Actual Balance:[/b] Lacking the talent to design genuinely fair encounters, the developers leaned entirely on magnetic, input-reading tracking. Bosses teleport across arenas and ignore spacing mechanics entirely to shut down tactical variety, forcing you into a single, rigid, utterly boring playstyle.

Black Myth: Wukong is a stunningly painted Ferrari with a lawnmower engine inside. It sacrifices crisp inputs, basic camera logic, player freedom, and world-building on the altar of visual spectacle. It is an insult to classic action games that actually respect a player’s skill and time. Do not waste your money on this overhyped tech demo. 

Uninstalling this garbage was the only satisfying part of the experience.

Rating: [b][u]Overwhelmingly Not Recommended[/u][/b]

Ahh, Black Myth: Wukong, a wonderfully made Chinese Soulslike that takes place after the Journey to the West novel, where if you have previously read said book, you will be able to catch a lot of the references the game made. I'll start off with graphics and performance. The game looks great, and for my pc, it ran smoothly. However, my old PC, which was a gaming laptop with a 3060, struggled to run this game on high settings. Granted, I was also trying to stream the game at the same time, so that had a factor on performance. I would say you do need a pretty beefy PC to run this game on high settings. Back to the game looking great, this game knows how to make a good spectacle. There are moments in the game, such as the second phase of Erlang's secret boss fight for the true ending, that are genuinely just badass. The combat is fun and satisfying, and you get plenty of spells, staffs, armors, and transformations to use throughout the game. Black Myth: Wukong isn't a particularly difficult soulslike, but it does have its fair share of bosses that are genuinely just plain annoying to fight, such as the Hundred-eyed Daoist and the Scorpionlord. Still, despite that, beating any boss in the game feels satisfying, as they're pretty much a nod to the 81 tribulations from the novel. That, and there are 81 bosses in total. As for the story itself, as I mentioned, it's a sequel to Journey to the West. The animations that is played for each chapter completed, especially the one for chapter 4's ending, are so beautifully made. Overall, Black Myth: Wukong is a great start to Game Science's Black Myth series, and I am super excited for their next game, Black Myth: Zhong Kui. 9/10!!! I love the Fat Buddha Baby. Oh, and do play this game with the Chinese voice acting. 🐵

《黑神话：悟空》是我入手的第一款单机 ARPG 游戏，同时也是这款游戏，带我真正进入了单机游戏世界。不过虽然是我的第一款动作游戏，但我上手游玩时却感觉意外的顺畅，玩起来并不觉得难（除了几个强敌），开始还以为我天赋异禀，直到后来我去玩了《只狼》，才明白自己当时有多天真。
       聊完小白视角的主观体验，接下来从更加专业的视角，聊聊它设计拔尖的地方。
       首先是它极致的战斗资源管理。气力和棍势的双重驱动，逼着玩家在每一次出招与闪避之间做出精密计算。轻攻击积攒棍势、识破化解危机、满豆瞬间重击释放，整套资源流转环环相扣，既没有纯数值堆砌的无脑换血，也没有无限制倾泻火力的廉价爽感，每一次体力见底前的停顿和棍势圆满后的决断，都充满了博弈的快感。
        其次是极其惊艳的中式美术风格。游戏里的场景完全不是那种廉价网游式的仙侠堆砌，那些实地古建扫描带来的石刻、残垣与悬塑佛像，一踏进去就扑面而来一股沉淀了千百年的厚重感。从陕北黄沙漫天的黄风岭，到雪花扑面、幽冷肃穆的小西天，每一处光影和材质的质感都扎实得不可思议。这种对中式古典美学的还原与重构，让跑图和探索不再只是单调的清怪赶路，而更像是一场沉浸感拉满的东方视觉巡礼。
       最后则是那些用心雕琢的过场动画。常有人说，玩硬核动作游戏受尽折磨，图的就是通关那一瞬间的“通关奖励”与情绪释放。而黑猴每一回打完奉上的章尾动画，就是制作组给玩家最顶级的通关馈赠。不管是黄眉诱人自相残杀的讽刺寓言，还是天蓬旧事里未了的执念，它们绝不是拿来敷衍交差的剧情过场，而是制作组掏出全部诚意奉上的一份厚礼。当你筋疲力尽、手心冒汗地磨死关底 Boss，靠在椅背上看着那一段段后劲十足、直击人心的艺术短片时，听着片尾响起的音乐，那种被巨大情绪包裹的爽快感，甚至超越了过关本身。对玩家来说，这才是最具含金量的通关正反馈。

作为首发花268元全价入手的玩家，看着《黑神话：悟空》开启30%限时折扣、标准版仅售187.6元，说心里毫无落差肯定不真实。但刷完两周目、摸透所有隐藏BOSS后回头看，这款国产3A标杆的成色，到底配不配得上原价，折扣期又值不值得入手，答案其实很清晰。
 
作为动作游戏，它的战斗体验绝对站在第一梯队。五套棍法各有风格，轻重攻击衔接、识破反击的反馈扎实厚重，三十余场BOSS战设计完全不重复，从白衣秀士到二郎神，每一场都有独特的阶段机制，初见的压迫感和通关后的成就感拉满。七十二变、法宝、精魄系统的加入，也让战斗策略足够丰富，多周目刷BOSS也不会很快乏味。
 
视听表现更是它的王牌。从苍莽的花果山到黄沙漫天的黄风岭，从诡谲的小雷音到盘丝洞，每一处场景都把东方古典美学拉到极致，怪物毛发、布料纹理、光影粒子的细节精度完全不输海外一线3A。全程中文配音搭配民乐配乐，把暗黑西游的氛围感焊死在每一秒里。
 
但它并非没有短板。没有小地图导致探索时容易迷路，部分大地图跑图略显枯燥，中低端显卡的优化问题至今仍有遗留，长时间游玩后动作模组的单一感也会逐渐显现。好在经过多轮更新，恶性BUG已基本修复，如今折扣期入手，体验反而比首发更完整顺滑。
 
回到最核心的价格问题：首发全价买入，买的是国产3A从零到一的里程碑意义，是第一时间沉浸西游世界的新鲜感；如今30%折扣，是新玩家以超高性价比入坑的最佳时机。
 
对于首发玩家，其实不必纠结降价——近六十小时的高质量内容，完全配得上原价。对于还在观望的人，七折的《黑神话：悟空》，绝对是闭眼入的水准。

[h1]黑神话：悟空——踏破虚妄与求道之路[/h1]

个人评价：S

我个人心目中的2024年度最佳游戏，作为国产 3A 的标杆，动画穿插水墨、木偶等国风形式，配乐与场景相得益彰，视听体验堪称顶尖。

[h1]剧情：A+[/h1]

它跳出传统取经框架，围绕轮回与执念重构西游世界观。影神图勾勒出众妖的过往，众生皆有悲苦，氛围感极强。但主线叙事碎片化，大量关键设定需要翻阅文本了解，剧情演出交代不足。结尾留白较多，主线节奏前稳后急，核心人物刻画偏少。设定想象力堪称顶尖，但主线故事完整性有所欠缺

[h1]氛围：S[/h1]

游戏把中式诡谲神话感做到极致，古寺残山、荒村古洞场景考究，妖怪造型取自壁画泥塑。搭配空灵又悲怆的配乐，环境音效层层烘托，孤寂、苍凉的宿命感扑面而来。水墨、木偶等动画短片进一步渲染意境。唯一不足是部分场景重复度偏高，但整体沉浸感极强，几乎从踏入花果山开始，就牢牢把人拉入这个悲凉的西游幻境

[h1]音乐：S[/h1]

游科把游戏配乐设计深度贴合东方神话气质，佛乐、民间小调与管弦乐融合，时而苍凉悲悯，时而雄浑肃杀。BOSS 战乐曲张力十足，山野间的清幽曲调又自带孤寂感。音效层次细腻，人声吟唱、法器铃音与环境音交织，和场景、剧情高度契合。少量配乐重复利用，但整体原创水准极高，完美烘托轮回虚妄的故事基调，是塑造游戏氛围感的核心支柱。

[h1]战斗系统和玩法：A[/h1]

以劈、立、戳三种棍势为核心，搭配识破、定身、分身与七十二变精魄系统，操作上限高，打法灵活。BOSS 设计风格迥异，招式富有压迫感。但 build 构建空间有限，装备技能搭配选择不多，后期部分小怪存在换皮。上手门槛适中，新手可依靠变身、法术降低难度，高手能钻研无伤连招，兼顾不同玩家，只是玩法深度距离顶级 ARPG 仍有差距。

[h1]内核：S[/h1]

游戏跳出传统西游叙事，以轮回、执念、真我为核心，重构东方哲思。神佛不再完美无瑕，妖魔各有悲苦宿命，打破非黑即白的善恶观。借天命人的旅途探讨挣脱虚妄、对抗宿命的精神，扎根于中国古典文化。这份厚重内核藏于影神图、场景隐喻之中，耐人反复品读。作为国产 3A，它把本土神话的精神力量用游戏载体传递出来，立意深邃，充满东方独有的浪漫与悲悯，足以称得上国产游戏内核表达的巅峰

[h1]细节和隐喻：S[/h1]

游戏各处遍布埋藏的伏笔，场景陈设、妖怪造型、影神图文字都暗藏隐喻。破败庙宇、残缺塑像暗示神佛的谎言与衰败；妖怪的身世细节，映射众生被执念捆绑的轮回困境。大量民俗、壁画、古籍元素融入场景，许多信息不会主动提示，需要玩家细心观察解读。诸多伏笔串联起整个世界观，多周目回看更能体会深意。美中不足是部分隐喻过于隐晦，容易被忽略，但庞大精巧的细节设计，让整个西游世界更具厚重感。
游戏是好游戏，就是为什么不能增加一个创意工坊呢，真的不想去其他网站下，打字必须给到5星，但是有那么多五星，我发上去也没人看呀，我给个一星。
三轮回了 地图也熟悉了 太好玩了 看我瑪喽子框框一顿锤

我认为《黑神话：悟空》是国产3A的一次巨大突破。游戏的国风场景、美术配乐十分惊艳，把西游神话那种苍凉诡谲的氛围完美呈现。战斗系统很有乐趣，棍势、识破、变身等机制丰富，挑战各路妖王时博弈感十足，打赢BOSS的成就感很强，影神图也补充了很多妖怪背后的故事。
 
但游戏也存在短板，全程没有小地图，很容易迷路。剧情叙事比较碎片化，只跑主线很难读懂完整故事。PC端对配置要求较高，部分场景会出现掉帧问题，后期小怪也有换皮重复的情况。整体瑕不掩瑜，适合喜欢动作游戏、对西游题材感兴趣的玩家。
夯中夯，趁着打折入手了，每天下班都要赶紧打开游戏，畅游！
挺好玩，难度也不是特别高。
玩过只狼后玩这个，纯爽游
夯爆了，没啥可说的，兄弟们！希望出副本，我要上天庭，救四妹！

之前电脑带不动，最近换了电脑才开始玩。
总体感觉还不错，就是遇到太多次出门就被埋伏磨血了。刚开始还没什么，次数多了就没意思了，还有精魄精炼不能和装备制作不能回炉返还就很难受
无法调难度，玩的我头昏眼胀不建议大家购买玩，我再也不玩黑神话悟空了！
难得的国产佳作，它是一个分水岭，开启了中国3A登上舞台的局面，战斗反馈很不错，但要熟练后，才可感受到最佳的战斗反馈(无线识破)

识破、退寸、秒定身、秒振刀、完美闪避、切棍，手感反馈特别好;剧情美术精彩;影神图故事伏笔都很精彩
四条龙是最好的陪练，法宝、精魄、变身、葫芦酒、丹药运用好事半功倍，如果你都学会了，就去打杨戬验收成果
第一次写评论，最爱无需多言
这是款很棒的游戏，它把中国的神话故事改编成了游戏，风景美，人物怪物建模奇特，故事设定哲学性强。在玩的过程中让人思考，反思自己人生过往未来。寻找六根，何尝不是人的六欲，寻找五蕴，到头来何不是皆空？
剧情设计，美术音乐，场景搭建，地图引导都属于一流，隐藏任务确实需要更加留意才能发现，但是做完会给人一种获得感，唯独几个boss（小黄龙、毒敌大王、大圣躯壳、二郎真君）难度设计有点超标。
打到花果山了，体验真的很棒，剧情画质没得挑。

从前读过今何在的《悟空传》和《西游日记》，书中那种对西游宿命的叩问，曾在心里留下很深的印记。而今踏入黑神话的天地，又是完全不一样的解读。
从黑风山古寺的虚妄贪念，踏入黄风岭漫天黄沙。原本以为只是斩妖除魔的旅途，却在一个个支线里看见众生。金池长老痴于袈裟，黄风大圣困于旧约，灵吉菩萨甘愿赴劫，一句“我之罪也”道尽其中纠葛。
寻蒲团，探隐世，解锁一桩桩劫难，才明白这个故事不只是西游的重述。妖有悲情，神有亏欠，世间善恶本就不是非黑即白。
神作，无需多言。
剧情优秀，难度可以接受
